chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may Allah be pleased with him) told us, saying: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Hamdani told us, saying: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal told us, from his father, saying: Al-Rida (peace be upon him) said:
Regarding the saying of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He: 'He is the One who shows you the lightning, out of fear and covet'
He said: Out of fear for the traveler, and out of covet for the lodging.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of fear and covet in the verse about lightning?
ai.summary: In Maani al-Akhbar, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates the dual nature of lightning in Surah Ar-Ra'd by distinguishing the psychological states of travelers and residents. This exegesis highlights the practical wisdom of the Imams in connecting divine signs to the specific socio-economic realities of 9th-century Arabia, where rain was a source of anxiety for nomads but a blessing for settled agriculturalists. Such interpretations underscore the Shia tradition of deriving nuanced, context-aware meanings from the Quranic text.
